mainEntity.name: What is different about Persian SEO?

acceptedAnswer.text: Half-spaces, digit forms and variant spellings of the same word affect search. We write with consistent spelling, based on the phrase your audience actually searches for.

mainEntity.name: Do you produce content with AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every published text is written, or rewritten and checked, by one of us, who takes responsibility for it. We do not produce filler articles. Marketing and content
Video, text, and SEO built from the same structure as the product, so content explains the work instead of decorating it.
Problem

items: Content made separately from the product tends to talk about everything except what the customer wants to know. Posts go out, and nobody knows which one answered a real customer question.

blocks.html: Who it is for

items: Businesses with a clear product that nobody finds in search.
Teams that want correctly written Persian content: half-spaces, digits and search intent.
Founders who need video or short text that explains the product, not general advertising.

blocks.html: Who it is not for

items: If you want a promised Google ranking. Nobody can honestly promise that.
If you want bought followers, fake engagement, or mass-produced filler articles.
If the product itself is not clear yet; in that case start with Business model design or UI/UX design.

blocks.html: Approach

items: Structure. Input: the product, its customers and their real questions. Output: a search intent map (which question is answered by which content, on which page). Owner: dadmor with you.
Plan. Input: the intent map. Output: a monthly content plan with channels. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
Produce. Input: the approved plan and access to the product or people. Output: content pieces (text, video), each approved before publishing. Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
Technical SEO. Input: your site. Output: a list of technical fixes (page titles and descriptions, structured data, speed, half-spaces and digits in Persian content). Owner: dadmor.
Report. Input: what was published and your analytics data. Output: a monthly report of what was published and what was measured. Owner: dadmor.

blocks.html: Deliverables
Scope and timeline factors

items: What changes the monthly band: pieces per month, type of piece (video takes the most work), number of channels, number of languages, and the amount of technical SEO work.
What you supply: access to the product and the people who know it, quick approval of drafts, and analytics access if you have it.
What delays the work: approvals that arrive late, and the product message changing mid-month.

blocks.html: Effort band

items: A monthly S, M or L band by pieces, channels and SEO work. We give a fixed monthly price after the scoping conversation, in a written proposal.

blocks.html: A band is the rough size of the work, not a price and not a duration. A fixed price is set only after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.
The band is a starting estimate; the scoping conversation may move it.
Limits and risks

items: We do not promise Google rankings. We deliver relevant content, correct structure and technical readiness; search results also depend on factors outside our control.
If you have no analytics, the monthly report can only say what was published, not what effect it had. We recommend privacy-friendly analytics.
Every piece needs your approval before publishing; we do not publish without it.
